verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents running incidents from Slack. Runbooks fire on declaration, automatically create the incident Slack channel and assign the opener as Commander, and responders post updates and browse runbooks via `/fh` commands inside the incident channel. However, no evidence shows the incident being declared from Slack itself, and Teams is never mentioned. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of declaring an incident from a Slack/Teams command, any Microsoft Teams support, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, I can declare and run an incident from chat — Slack or Teams — with channels, roles, and updates created for me

citations.quote: Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
**Assign a Role**: Assigns whoever opened the incident to the Commander role.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
From Slack, inside an incident channel, you can browse the list of triggered Runbooks for this by executing `/fh`.
All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
